In traditional FA, the AHG model is incorporated which enhances convergence speed rapidly. It increases decision-making and ensures optimal performance and allocation. The objective function is controlled to EV reachability with obtainable State of Charge (SoC) to the selected charging station by without irrelevant maximum allowable depth of discharge limit which enable for charging rate. The optimization approach allows the users for prioritizing the variable function depending on battery specifications in various analysis. The proposed AHG-FA achieves a minimum total time of 55.21 m compared to existing techniques such as AHG-Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), AHG-Pelican Optimization Algorithm (POA), AHG-Bald Eagle Optimization (BEO) and AHG-Butterfly Optimization Algorithm (BOA).

Author Keywords: adaptive heuristic guidance based firefly approach

articleTitle: Multi-Parent Crossover Strategy based African Vulture Optimization for Safer Emergency Evacuations in Optimal Placement of Exit Doors
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The optimal placement of exit doors for the evacuations of safer emergency emphases on strategically locating departure during emergencies to reduce evacuation time and increase safety. By applying crowd simulation approach assists to determine passenger behavior and movement in different scenarios and identifies potential bottlenecks. However, ensuring safe and effective emergency evacuations in crowded scenes rises from suboptimal placement of exit door that results in congestion and enhanced times. This research proposes Multi-Parent Crossover Strategy based African Vulture Optimization (MPCS-AVO) to increase placement of exit doors for safer emergency evacuations. In traditional AVO, the MPCS mechanism is incorporated to enhance exploitation stage which generates solutions with more varieties and increase solution quality. The proposed MPCS-AVO represents the exit door’s optimum location for a multi-room situation to enhance the evacuation effectiveness by reducing crowd evacuation times. The proposed MPCS-AVO achieves a better execution time of 9.67 s compared to existing techniques like Golden Jackal Optimization (GJO), Social Spider Algorithm (SSA), Sun Flower Optimization (SFO), and AVO.

articleTitle: Sleep Quality Prediction and Estimation by using Deep Belief Networks-Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Sufficient sleep is important for individuals who are suffering with chronic diseases, as sleep scarcity severely impacts emotional, physical and mental well-being, worsening health complications. The existing convolutional network for sleep quality prediction and estimation has computational complexity and over fitting by which the model didn’t effectively predict the quality of sleep. Therefore, this research proposes Deep Belief Networks-Bayesian Optimization (DBN-BO) for predicting and estimating the quality of sleep. Initially, Sleep study data is used as input and this data contains outliers which are preprocessed by using local outlier factor and effectively reduced impact of noise while detecting the outliers. Then, the sleep quality is predicted by using DBN which learns the complex features from raw data. After that, BO is used for estimating the quality of sleep and explores the various factors related to sleep. This proposed DBN-BO effectively reduced the computational complexity and over fitting by training one layer at a time, proposed DBN-BO achieved better results in terms of accuracy $\mathbf{9 4 . 4 5 \%}$, sensitivity $\mathbf{9 7 . 0 9 \%}$, and specificity of $\mathbf{9 3 . 4 5 \%}$ and F1-Score of $91.12 \%$ when compared with existing convolutional layers.

articleTitle: A Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit and Long Short-Term Memory based Fake Profile Identification System
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Nowadays, fake profiles are programmatically created online individualities that mislead and influence others, which are done by frequently using stolen photos, fraudulent information, or fictional particulars. Hence, these fake profiles are used for malicious activities such as phishing, social engineering, catfishing, and scattering misinformation. The expansion of fake profiles is increased with triggering more damage than any other cyber-attacks. The solution has been recommended in various ways to detect fake profiles, but the existing models have more overfitting problems. To overcome these issues, a combined model of Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithms is proposed. Initially, data preprocessing is done on TwiBot-20 dataset with Natural Language Processing (NLP) and tokenization to remove unnecessary characters. Next, a word embedding technique name called GloVe is used to extract the optimal features, Finally, from the extracted features, the proposed BiGRU-LSTM model gives a precise rate in detecting and classifying fake profiles as human and bot generated. The proposed BiGRU-LSTM gives better results than the other compared existing methods Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and f1 score of $99.73 \%, 98.23 \%, 99.56 \%$, and $99.63 \%$ respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing Intrusion Detection Systems for 5G Networks using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: As 5G networks advance, cybersecurity vulnerabilities in IoT devices are increasingly exposed. While intrusion detection systems (IDS) have progressed, there is a notable gap in IDS specifically designed for the unique protocols and complexities of 5G networks. Current research often emphasises binary classification, missing the nuanced multiclass classification needed for effective threat detection. This study addresses these deficiencies by integrating machine learning and deep learning techniques within the 5G core architecture to develop an advanced IDS. Utilising TCP/IP flow statistics and PFCP signalling attack data, and focusing on control plane signalling between the Session Management Function (SMF) and User Plane Function (UPF), various models are evaluated for detecting anomalous activities. The study achieves 97% accuracy with TCP/IP data and 69% with PFCP data. The proposed IDS, tailored for 5G-specific workloads and trained on PFCP protocol data, enhances detection capabilities and addresses significant security challenges, improving the resilience of IoT devices in 5G networks.

articleTitle: Innovative Approaches to Real-Time Occlusion Handling for Enhanced Augmented Reality Experiences
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Occlusion is a critical aspect of augmented reality and mixed reality systems, profoundly impacting realism and the user experience. This research paper explores various techniques and optimizations to generate better occlusion output on augmented and mixed reality systems in real time, the proposed techniques helped us build better occlusion effects suitable for dynamic environmental objects and human subjects. Our approach successfully integrated dynamic and stable occlusion through the integration of Lightship ARDK which leverages the depth sensors in real-time producing stable occlusions. Additionally, various optimizations were applied to enhance occlusion output without sacrificing performance or accuracy. Notably, the implementation of occlusion by semantically segmenting and suppressing unwanted objects from the environment yielded better results compared to other techniques, which further improved upon the performance of the occlusion on mobile devices.

articleTitle: Innovative Predictive Modeling for Tailored Cirrhosis Management Unveiling Novel Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The severe scarring of the liver due to the scar tissue gradually replacing healthy liver tissue results in Cirrhosis. This leads to liver failure, portal hypertension, and liver cancer. Our research uses advanced machine learning models with innovative null handling and feature engineering strategies to enhance predictive accuracy. We apply techniques such as iterative SVM-based imputation and groupwise median imputation, leveraging group-specific statistics to handle missing data, alongside feature selection algorithms to extract informative features. Additionally, we propose the ALBI_SCORE, a novel feature based on clinical insights to boost predictive performance. Stratified 20-fold cross-validation was employed to fine-tune hyperparameters, ensuring robustness and generalizability. Key metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and AUROC were used to evaluate the models. Our study found that the GroupWise median imputation technique achieved 90% accuracy, while the SVM-based imputation method achieved 84%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in predicting cirrhosis outcomes.

articleTitle: Improved Recurrent Convolutional Neural Network for Crack Detection in Concrete Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)

authors.preferredName: R Rana Veer Samara Sihman Bharattej

abstract: Detecting cracks in concrete structures involves advanced imaging and deep learning techniques to identify and assess the extent of structural damage. The problem statement in crack detection methods like an identification of cracks, complex background noise, intricate patterns, and environmental conditions are overcome by segmentation and detection process of this approach. The SDNet2018 dataset and the proposed crack detection method, like U-Net for segmentation, distinguish between cracks and non-cracks. Inception ResNetV2 for pixel-wise feature extraction enhances the identification of crack patterns. The final step involves crack-type detection using an Improved Recurrent Convolutional Neural Network (RCNN). The proposed method achieves performance metrics with an accuracy of $99.67 \%$, precision of $98.78 \%$, recall of $99.45 \%$, and an F1-score of ${9 9. 2 1 \%.}$ Existing methods like Convolutional Neural Network (CNN+U-Net), K-means with Genetic Algorithm (GKA), Multiscale Crack Detection Network (MSCNet), and Transfer Learning (TL) overcome limitations and provide accurate solution for crack detection in surface areas.

articleTitle: Cognitive Digital Twin Systems for Predictive Security in AI-Enhanced IoT Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The Internet has grown in importance and impact over the years, causing people to become more reliant on it. The Internet has evolved into a major vector for cybercrime because to its ever-increasing user base. Over the last decade, the number of these computing systems—including desktops, laptops, smartphones, and the Internet of Things (IoT)—has skyrocketed. Among them, cell phones are practically integral to modern life. The popularity of web-based assaults has skyrocketed with the exponential growth in the number of individuals using the Internet. These web-based assaults are increasingly being combatted by security corporations. Unfortunately, new forms of these assaults are appearing all the time, making it hard for older security measures to stay up. Artificial intelligence (AI) is a source of optimism in the current cybersecurity landscape, offering a potential solution to the ever-changing digital dangers. The fast development of AI over the last decade has given rise to this optimism, because it is now impacting the expansion of every industry. With AI bringing so many advantages in every field, online security is one sector that just cannot afford to ignore it. This thesis represents progress in that direction. This thesis covers research that aims to use AI to tackle significant online security challenges. Security in Internet of Things (IoT) settings powered by artificial intelligence may be improved with the help of cognitive digital twin systems (CDTS). In order to provide proactive security measures, real-time monitoring, and predictive analysis, these systems use cutting-edge AI methods to digitally represent physical IoT devices. In order to anticipate and lessen the impact of security risks, this research introduces a new CDTS architecture that combines cognitive learning skills, anomaly detection, and machine learning models. The suggested approach reduced reaction time to security events by 87.5% and identified zero-day threats with a detection accuracy of $\mathbf{9 2. 4 \%}$ by using cognitive computing and predictive security measures. The findings prove that the CDTS architecture is a strong answer to adaptive and intelligent threat management, and they show how well it secures complicated IoT networks.

articleTitle: Deep Separable Dilated Convolutional Neural network for Cloud Detection and Removal in Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The satellite is observation activities such as urban and agricultural and disaster management are constrained by adequate spatial and temporal ground observation. The detecting clouds data is usually distort ground optical observation and reduce the temporal resolution it degrades the learning valuable information. The significantly impacted by the presence of pixels affected by cloud and showdown of the cloud. This paper, proposed Lightweight Deep Separable Dilated Convolutional Neural network (DS-DCNN) technique is efficiently performed in the cloud detection removed from the satellite imagery. The data collected from the Sentinel-2 Satellite dataset and pre-processing involved the minmax normalization and uniformly scale the feature vector. Data augmentation is process to detecting various of clouds data and enhance the presences of training data to handling difficult of the satellite imagery. The DS-DCNN technique efficiently detecting clouds of varying sizes and shapes of the image from the different satellite dataset and capture global structure of satellite image and removed unwanted data. The performance of improved Deep Learning (DL) model evaluated the various metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Square Error (MSE), Root-Mean-Squared Error (RMSE) Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) metrics on Sentinel-2 Satellite dataset.

Author Keywords: lightweight deep separable dilated convolutional neural network and satellite imagery

articleTitle: Image Recognition in the Kitchen: A Novel Approach to Meal Planning with Accuplate
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Innovative image recognition technology is revolutionizing meal planning and cooking through web applications that identify ingredients from food images and generate recipe suggestions. The proposed system, powered by deep learning and advanced image recognition, follows a multi-step process including image preprocessing, feature extraction, and ingredient recognition, culminating in personalized recipe generation. After extensive training on diverse food images, the web app demonstrates high accuracy in recognizing both common and uncommon ingredients, offering tailored meal suggestions that cater to various dietary needs. The system encourages users to explore new dishes, promotes healthy eating, and significantly reduces meal preparation time. Despite its benefits, the app faces challenges such as image quality and the need for a continuously updated ingredient database. Overall, the web app represents a major advancement in meal planning, providing an efficient and user-friendly solution for healthier and more creative cooking experiences.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Technique for Mobility and Signal Strength-Based Route Selection in MANET
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: A mobile ad hoc network is a collection of movable nodes that are capable of facilitating a route that requires a source node and transmitting the data using multipoint communication. The node uses energy for operation, but its lifespan is limited, necessitating the implementation of techniques to extend its communication lifetime. Many studies have proposed energy and mobility-based communication to increase the lifetime using various methods, but a better technique is still needed. In this paper, we integrate the AODV with machine learning (ML) technique, which gathers data from all nodes regarding their energy and mobility values. This data is then used to predict a more efficient route from the source to the destination node. The combination of machine learning with AODV routing minimizes the route failure ratio and increases the network life time. In the proposed section, we elucidate how the machine learning utilizes input parameters such as energy, mobility, and signal strength to select the optimal route. The results section looks at how well the proposed machine learning system works with the min-max battery cost routing (MMBCR) and receiving signal strength routing protocol (RSS-RP). We find that the proposed system does a better job in terms of throughput, energy use, residual energy, PDR, delay, and overhead. It concludes that the proposed ML-AODV increases the lifetime of the MANET network.

articleTitle: Next-Gen Threat Detection: Leveraging AI and Cyber Twin Technologies for IoT Security
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has led to a surge in cyber threats, demanding the development of robust security frameworks. This paper introduces an advanced threat detection model, leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Cyber Twin Technologies for enhanced IoT security. The proposed framework integrates a Cyber Twin-a digital replica of physical IoT devices-with real-time data analytics to detect, predict, and respond to sophisticated cyber-attacks. The Cyber Twin continuously monitors IoT networks, identifying abnormal behaviors and enabling the implementation of dynamic security measures through AI-driven intrusion detection systems (IDS). A hybrid deep learning approach combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) is utilized to enhance anomaly detection and threat classification accuracy. The system’s ability to simulate various attack scenarios within a digital environment facilitates the development of effective countermeasures while minimizing the impact on actual IoT operations. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in detection accuracy, reduced false positives, and enhanced system resilience. The proposed AI and Cyber Twin-based threat detection model sets a new benchmark in safeguarding IoT infrastructures against emerging cyber threats. Experimental results show a detection accuracy of 96.2%, a 35% reduction in response time, and a 15% reduction in false positives compared to traditional rule-based methods. Additionally, the system demonstrated 98.1% resilience against simulated attacks, setting a new benchmark in safeguarding IoT infrastructures against emerging cyber threats.

articleTitle: Insider Threat Detection and its Behavior with Excessive Access Privileges
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Insider threats, one of the most challenging cyber threats, often result in significant organizational losses. This study explores the correlation between suspicious users and job roles vulnerable to insider threats. The research highlights that users with higher access privileges are more exposed to potential insider attacks. K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and hierarchical clustering, implemented using Weka, were employed to detect suspicious activity and group users by their roles. Based on a comparison of successive months, an overall accuracy value of 0.85 was obtained. By monitoring for suspicious changes in their cluster over time, we were able to identify 80% of insider threats with the ITAdmin job. The results revealed that many users exhibiting abnormal activities held IT admin roles, indicating that those with the highest access permissions are more prone to insider threats. This study addresses a gap in understanding the relationship between excessive access permissions and security risks.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis in Code-Mixed Video Comments Using Machine Learning on a Hinglish Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Given the fluency of user-created information across languages, colloquialisms, and cultural nuances the task of sentiment analysis in code-mixed video comments is challenging. In this study, sentiment analysis of bilingual (English-Hindi) comments from YouTube, Instagram, and other video-sharing platforms has received considerable importance. To address these problems, we created a large set of code-mixed comments collected from various sites. Employing the voting technique, we also combined machine learning algorithms, including the Random Forest and Logistic Regression algorithms, along with NLP to form an ensemble machine learning model. This made it possible to extract subtleties from the bilingual text with a superb $\mathbf{9 1 \%}$ sentiment classification accuracy. In this work, it was revealed that the use of advanced models for code-mixed text, audience engagement tactics recommended content tactics, and content moderation strategies in well-used video platforms may be significantly improved. The findings show that audience engagement tactics, targeted recommendations, and content moderation on wellknown video platforms may all be considerably enhanced by utilizing sophisticated models designed for code-mixed text. This work lays the groundwork for future multilingual sentiment analysis research, and our dataset can be an invaluable tool for developing the discipline.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Heart Disease Detection using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Machine Learning is a state-of-art technology applied widely in various sectors including health care and has made significant advancements in this field by revolutionizing diagnostic and treatment approaches. Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) have remained a leading global cause of death witnessed across the world. However, early detection of this disease has proven crucial for improving patient health outcomes. In this context, the current study has investigated the use of machine learning models to predict cardiovascular disease risk by examining clinical and lifestyle factors, including age, gender, blood pressure, cholesterol and glucose levels, smoking habits, and alcohol consumption. Six different machine learning models are trained and tested over the available data from Kaggle. The built models are evaluated based on various performance metrics including accuracy score, training time, F1-Score, recall, etc. The final inference of the study is that the decision tree models, particularly, random forest and gradient boosting algorithms proved to be more accurate among all other models used in this study. The research emphasized how these machine learning techniques have improved early diagnosis and facilitated timely interventions, helping healthcare providers make more informed decisions and ultimately enhanced patient care.

articleTitle: Enhancing SAR Automatic Target Recognition with Advanced Target Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: These are the novel approaches taken by us to minimize the hurdles ATR poses for SAR systems. Thus, we designed ATGAN-an Advanced Target Generative Adversarial Network with a dual-network architecture toward image generation realistic for SAR target generation. Substantial experimentations have improved the recognition accuracy and robustness as well, compared with traditional models like SVM, KNN and LSTM networks. The performance metrics of ATGAN are truly phenomenal; the sensitivity score was $0.9998 \%$, specificity at $0.9997 \%$, and an accuracy of $0.9999 \%$. Its F1 value had reached an incredible value of $\mathbf{0. 9 9 9 6 \%}$ to show its excellent balance between precision and recall. The SVM, KNN, and LSTM models scored perfectly well but were a couple of notches behind in the critical parameters of ATGAN. Results show that the ATGAN-based approach outperformed methods reported in literature for SAR ATR tasks, especially in complex and dynamic environments where accuracy is of high priority.

articleTitle: Medical Document Classification using NLP Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The field of medicine is a vital functional block in our lives. It is also now a growing domain in machine learning and text-based classification. This opens up a world of possibilities for enhancing patient care, clinical decision-making, and medical research. However, the large number and diversity of medical records, present significant hurdles in efficiently organizing and extracting valuable insights from these extensive records. Manual sorting and retrieval of medical text can be exhausting, time-consuming, and error-prone, highlighting the need for automated solutions to improve the general quality of life for performing these operations [19]. Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods have potential to be good tools for analyzing and classifying text records across various fields.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Wastewater Treatment using Feedforward Neural Network and Batch Normalization
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: In present scenario, the freshwater is a contest as the world’s population raises. Most of Earth’s water comes from brackish water and seawater those are the largest sources of water. Water purification is crucial during this water crisis, and can be achieved through desalination and various water treatment techniques, making water safe for human consumption and other uses. Wastewater treatment downsides including with high energy consumption and chemical usage in mixture of water. Limited removal of certain pollutants sludge generation release are also concerns which are included with various pollutants with concern of overfitting leads to the overreliance on a specific treatment. To overcome these issues, the method of (Feedforward Neural Network (FFNN) and Batch Normalization (BN) (FFNN-BN)) is proposed by collecting water pollutants. This process involves with the collection of input from the dataset of Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) and then features are extracted by proposed method FF-BN and classifying extracted features by the SVR handles high-dimensional data with a large number of features. The proposed FFNN-BN produce more results than traditional methods of Advanced Oxidation Processes (AOP) for modeling extreme values such as R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) respectively.

articleTitle: Boosting Reweighting Convolutional Neural Network for Microscopic Images to Identify and Classify Malaria Parasites
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Malaria is a critical health condition that affects both sultry and frigid region worldwide, its rise to millions of cases disease. The malaria is caused by parasites through to pass in the human blood cells, damage them over the time and occur the noise because it blends in the human blood cells. Therefore, it is identifying by using microscope Image to exanimated the blood cells. This paper, proposed Boosting Reweighting Convolutional Neural Network (BR-CNN) technique efficiently analysis the region to malaria parasites classify the disease image. Data obtained from the NIH Malaria dataset and pre-processing utilized remove unwanted noise in the image and normalization of the feature vector. The feature extraction involved the ResNet 50 utilized residual connections, which allows gradients to flow through the network, effectively extracted the malaria parasites. The Classification utilized BR-CNN technique is automatically extract features from the input blood cell image. The CNN processes the image through layer of the convolutional operations and non-linear activation to build a hierarchical representation of data. The performance of proposed model evaluated the various metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and sensitivity metrics on NIH dataset.

articleTitle: Predicting Stress, Anxiety, and Depression from Social Media Comments: A Holistic Multi-Modal Deep Learning and NLP Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: In the current digital era, millions of people are affected by increased levels of stress, anxiety, and desperation making mental health a critical worldwide concern. Proactive approaches to early detection of these illnesses are necessary to address this dilemma. This research aims to create a mental health condition prediction model by utilizing deep learning, machine learning, and natural language processing (NLP) cutting edge methods. We use social media data to identify potential red flags for mental health issues early on. To build a strong framework, our suggested approach combines classic machine learning techniques like Random Forest and SVMs with neural networks, such as CNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs. Through an examination of language patterns and behaviors seen in social media content, our models provide insights into current trends in mental health. Experimental results demonstrate high predictive accuracy, highlighting the potential for early intervention. This research addresses the growing need for innovative, data-driven approaches to mental health care, facilitating timely support, personalized treatment, and improved outcomes for individuals and communities.

articleTitle: Federated Learning-Based Network Slicing in 6G Systems for Enhanced Performance in Autonomous Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: To improve 6G connectivity for autonomous vehicles (AVs), this article suggests a network slicing system based on federated learning. AVs maintain privacy by using federated learning to train models locally on communication data, and then aggregate a global model without exchanging raw data. The system dynamically distributes network slices to satisfy real-time communication requirements, including interactions between vehicles and infrastructure V2I and V2V. Numerous simulations show significant gains, such as a $\mathbf{5. 2 ~ m s}$ latency reduction, 100.5 Mbps throughput increase, and 99.7% dependability improvement. With a score of 94.2%, privacy is protected while resource consumption is minimized to 85.4%. These findings show that, in comparison to more conventional approaches, the suggested architecture provides better performance and data safety while meeting the demanding specifications of 6G-enabled AV communication.

Author Keywords: objective modular network testbed in c++

articleTitle: An Underwater Object Detection and Tracking using Bounding Box Prediction and Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Nowadays, an Object detection and tracking stays energetic and inspiring task in present processer imagination with extensive applications in various industries such as investigation, independent robot directions, and vehicle navigation. The increase in availability of computing power and vast public datasets has made it possible to develop and train robust object identification and tracking systems, driving innovation and advancements in these fields of tracking objects. Object detection faces several challenges such as, where objects are partially or fully hidden by other objects, and variation in pose and scale, which affects an object's appearance. Cluttered backgrounds and changing lighting conditions are also make detection difficult. To overcome these issues, the method of Convolutional Neural Network for Underwater (UW) Object Detection and Tracking (CNN-UWODT) is proposed with DenseNet feature extraction and bounding box for tracking the objects. The process involves with collecting input images from UOT-32 dataset converting to frames extracting features with DenseNet; then predicting the bounding boxes with CNN, and classifying objects with Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (KELM) component to identify key metrics from the input data. The proposed CNN-UWODT presents better results than the traditional You Only Look Once, Version 3 (YOLO-V3)in terms of precision ($94 \%$), recall ($96 \%$) and f1 score ($95 \%$) respectively.

articleTitle: Monitoring in-Vehicle Air Quality in Real Time Through IoT and Enhanced Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Globally, air pollution (AP) is among the most pressing environmental crises. With human health in mind, numerous researchers have focused on these issues. Predictive data on air quality is one of the most effective means of alerting the public to the dangers of air pollution and encouraging them to take preventative measures. One of the most difficult environmental problems in many large cities is air pollution. Preprocessing, feature selection, and model training are the three stages that make up the process. Data scaling, pollution comparison, and status fixing are all parts of preprocessing. The process of feature selection makes use of Q-learning based bee swarm optimization. The model was trained using an A-CNN-LSTM-XGBoost. With an average accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 6 1 \%}$, the suggested method outperforms LSTM and A-CNN.

articleTitle: Escherichia Coli Bacterial Identification using Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs), predominantly caused by Uro-Pathogenic Escherichia Coli (UPEC), account for 80% of cases, posing a significant health challenge. Traditional methods for bacterial identification, such as culturing, are both time-consuming and costly. In this study, a Deep Learning (DL) approach using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model developed with TensorFlow’s Keras API is presented to quickly and accurately identify E. coli and non-E. coli bacteria colonies from a custom dataset of 978 images collected using mobile devices. The model, comprising three convolutional layers (32, 64, and 128 filters), was trained for 30 epochs, achieving 91% accuracy. Max pooling, dropout layers, $\mathbf{L} 2$ regularization and early stopping was implemented to prevent overfitting. Data augmentation was also applied to enhance model generalization. The findings demonstrate that this cost-effective, real-time deep learning method provides an efficient alternative to conventional identification techniques, offering a promising tool for rapid diagnostics in clinical environments.

articleTitle: Leveraging Context for Enhanced Emotion Recognition: A Study Using SSD with ResNet
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The increasing interest in automated emotional state recognition systems presents significant potential for applications in human-machine interactions and monitoring. Nonetheless, conventional methods that concentrate on facial expressions and body language for emotion recognition often disregard the substantial variations stemming from cultural and situational contexts. This paper addresses the limitations of conventional emotion recognition methods, which often overlook cultural and situational context. We propose an extension to the system introduced in “Context-Based Emotion Recognition using the EMOTIC Dataset” to classify and detect 19 out of 26 emotions. Our approach leverages Single Shot Detectors (SSD) like ResNet50 and ResNet-101 as backbones. Using a subset of EMOTIC dataset consisting of 9,000 images, our model, based on SSD with ResNet-50 and a batch size of 8, we achieved an 8% higher recall than the second-best model and a 35% improvement over the worst. We also address dataset bias and propose improved annotation metrics. This research highlights the critical role of context in emotion recognition and the potential of context-aware deep learning for human-computer interaction and monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Effective Prognosis of Heart Attack Using Supervised Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Early identification of heart attack is essential and predicting it using clinical data is a complex process due to the multifaceted nature of the disease and the diverse range of contributing factors. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms are powerful tools for predicting heart disease by analyzing patient healthcare data. This paper explores the predictive analysis of heart attack using supervised ML algorithms: Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Classification and Regression Tree (CART), and Random Forest (RF) algorithms. AdaBoost is a simple ensemble algorithm that improves the performance of weak learners by focusing on misclassified instances. CART is highly interpretable and efficient in handling non-linear data relationships. Random Forest is a robust algorithm that aggregates the predictions of multiple decision trees to produce accurate predictions. A comprehensive dataset comprising various cardiovascular health indicators is used to evaluate these algorithms. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms significantly enhance prediction accuracy upto 96%.

articleTitle: Automated Brain Abnormality Segmentation using Modified JAYA algorithm based Fuzzy C-Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The main risk factors in humans, irrespective of gender or location, are anomalies of the brain, such as tumors and strokes. In healthcare facilities, the degree of disability and underlying cause of brain lesions are typically evaluated by means of regular methods created by trained clinicians. During this procedure, signals and images of the brain are collected in a controlled setting. Selecting an appropriate separation method is essential to getting the desired results. The novel JAYA algorithm, which relies on meta-heuristics, aids in the reclustering of the FCM segmentation results in our suggested techniques, yielding more productive delineation results with clear borders with 86% of Dice Score. However, the exploitation and exploration techniques for searching become more flexible and help identify the optimal solution faster by adjusting the desired function with respect to the accommodating cluster location and population size. Regarding the processing speed, optimal exploitation, and exploratory abilities, the suggested strategy outperforms the other available metaheuristic optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Advanced E-Waste Management Solutions using A-BiCNN-RNN Model to Tackle Modern Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: As a term, “e-waste” refers to the trash produced by the disposal of electronic devices such as old phones, computers, and televisions. As far as waste management problems go, online trash is quickly becoming one of the biggest ones. The concerning increase of electronic garbage is due to numerous causes. Included in this category are developments in technology, the frequency with which products break, shifts in customer taste, and the use of intentional obsolescence in product design to increase profits through increased product turnover. The rapid increase in worldwide e-waste output is a major threat to both the environment and human health, making efficient e-waste treatment a critical need. However, low recycling rates and large yearly e-waste production make effective management of discarded electronics a major challenge in developing nations. Preprocessing, feature selection, and training the model are the three stages that make up the process. Reverse filling is a preprocessing technique that is used to find and remove empty cells. One popular method for extracting features is Linear Discriminant Analysis, or LDA. The A-BiCNN-RNN was utilized for the model’s training. Compared to Attention models and RNNs, the proposed technique achieves a higher average accuracy of $\mathbf{9 3. 4 7 \%}$.

articleTitle: Modelling & Simulation of Multi-Path OTAs with Dual Flipped Voltage Follower for VLSI based DSP Applications using 50nm Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The article introduces the designing and simulation of Multi-Path Fully Operational Transconductance Amplifiers (OTAs) featuring a Dual Flipped Voltage Follower (DFVF), specifically optimized for VLSI-based digital signal processing (DSP) applications. The design is implemented using 50nm CMOS technology and simulated using Cadence tools. By incorporating multiple signal paths, the proposed OTA architecture improves bandwidth, gain, and linearity, while effectively reducing common-mode noise. The research successfully demonstrates the modeling and simulation of Multi-Path OTAs with DFVF configurations using 50 nm CMOS technology. The results show significant improvements in key performance areas such as bandwidth, gain, linearity, and noise reduction. However, the study also acknowledges some limitations, including the reliance on the 50 nm technology node and the lack of real-world validation. While simulation results are encouraging, further testing is required to validate the OTA’s performance in practical applications. Despite these constraints, the proposed OTA design represents a stable and efficient solution with strong potential for integration into modern VLSI systems, demonstrating its value in high-performance signal processing.

articleTitle: Kidney Stone Classification using Machine Learning Models on CT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Crystalline masses, better known as kidney stones, develop inside the kidneys and lead to severe pains and further complications if not detected timely. Robust and precise kidney stones classification from CT images is critical for the diagnosis and treatment process. This work explores the usage of diverse machine learning models for kidney stone type detection (KNN, Naive Bayes and Neural Network). The dataset employed consists of 4 categories CT images including Cyst, Normal, Stone and Tumor. Preprocessing steps also included resizing images to $128 \times 128$ pixels and converting them into black and white. Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) features were extracted to obtain structural information from the images. The models were measured on 80-20% of training and test sets, with the performance metrics considering accuracy precision recall F1-score. The Neural Network model has obtained the best accuracy of 0.99 and also outperformed than KNN as well Naive Bayes. The KNN model also had significant results and an accuracy of 0.99 whereas the Naive Bayes classifier struggled with lower accuracy, performance metrics etc.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Approach for Efficient 3D Object Detection in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The YOLOv3 deep learning architecture is utilized in this project to develop an advanced framework for 3D object detection in vehicle automation. This technology ensures precise and rapid detection of essential objects like cars, pedestrians, and barriers, crucial for safe autonomous driving. By integrating 2D bounding boxes with 3D coordinate estimations, the system analyzes input from multiple sensors to identify and classify various elements in the driving environment. This capability is vital for navigating complex scenarios that require swift decision-making, particularly in urban settings, highways, and unpredictable traffic. A primary objective is to enhance computational efficiency for real-time applications, achieving an impressive 89.55% detection accuracy. Performance evaluations demonstrate the system’s adaptability across diverse conditions, including varying lighting, weather, and road types. The combination of 3D object recognition and rapid processing positions this framework as a key advancement in developing reliable and secure automated vehicles.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization of Cloud Intelligent Logistics Control System based on GBDT and LSTM Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: In order to achieve the goal of “carbon neutrality and carbon peak”, this paper investigates the optimization method of cloud-based intelligent logistics regulation system based on GBDT and LSTM neural network. We developed a new logistics information transportation optimization and sharing platform - “the most ‘optimal’ transportation”, which integrates a real-time distribution route optimization system and a special travel strategy speed distribution system. The platform adopts GBDT algorithm, simulated annealing algorithm, Logistic’s SUE model, entropy weight TOPSIS method, LSTM neural network, ray tracing method and blockchain technology to realize real-time tracking of logistics transportation, optimization of distribution routes, lowering of logistics costs, and reduction of carbon emissions. Through the analysis of the current situation of the logistics industry at home and abroad and the in-depth study of the development plan of modern logistics, we have explored the path of green transformation of the logistics industry, and provided a scientific and practical solution to achieve the goal of “double carbon”. The research results show that the platform can effectively improve the efficiency and quality of logistics services and contribute to the construction of ecological civilization and sustainable development.

articleTitle: Predictions of Basketball Match Results using Autoencoder with Gated Recurrent Unit Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: This research explores basketball match predictions within the field of sports analytics utilized Deep Learning (DL) technique to analyse the outcomes of National Basketball Association (NBA) games based on player performance and team statistics. The challenge in predicting NBA games outcomes and performance analysis various factor, as the high dimensionality of the data and uncertainty surrounding player due to difficult to predictions of basketball game. This paper, proposed Autoencoder with Gated Recurrent Unit (AE-GRU) algorithm to efficiently analyse and predict NBA game outcomes. The data was initially collected from NBA games between 2009 - 2021, focusing on five teams and pre-processing involved min-max normalization to uniformly scale the feature vectors. The Principal Component Analysis (PCA) utilized for feature selection, effectively reducing the high dimensionality of the NBA game data across various teams. The AE-GRU technique then captured the complex feature of basketball game data and handled uncertainty data and enhances performance. The performance of DL model evaluated the various metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score metrics on NBA game.

Author Keywords: predictions of basketball and principal component analysis

articleTitle: Information Extraction Algorithms and Semantic Understanding in Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Complex natural language texts affect the accuracy of information extraction and semantic understanding. To address this problem, this paper applies the attention mechanism to make full use of contextual information to solve the problems of ambiguity and contextual understanding. Deep learning technology is used to process complex syntactic structures. This paper explores how to apply the theory of information extraction and semantic understanding to various practical problems, and provides new ideas for improving the efficiency and quality of natural language processing. Through this study, the accuracy, robustness and accuracy of information extraction and semantic understanding have all been improved, with the highest valuesof the three indicators being $95.9 \%, \quad 0.90 \%$ and $97.9 \%$ respectively.

articleTitle: Service Function Chain Deployment and Optimization at the Network Edge: An Application of A3C Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: NFV technology deploies network functions on a universal server, and constructs management and orchestration modules to create and delete VNF and its resources. This provides a way to realize the virtual resource orchestration function of SFC orchestration system. The Actor-Critic algorithm combines two types of reinforcement learning algorithms, PolicyGradient and value-based Q-learning. A3C algorithm has been proved to have better convergence, and it performs better in high-dimensional and continuous space. Deep reinforcement learning has strong perception ability and decision-making ability at the same time, and the effect is stable and good in the face of various complex mobile edge computing problems. Dynamic service function chaining can adaptively set and adjust SFCs to ensure service continuity when users move. This paper presents the novel methods of service unction chain deployment and optimization at the network edge: an application of A3C algorithm. Finally, a comparison is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed new algorithm. The experimental results show that $\mathrm{A3C}$ algorithm is better than DDPG algorithm in SFC placement efficiency.

articleTitle: Virtual Circuit based Real Time Wearable Device for Alerting Erroneous Neck Posture
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: This Due to the increasing use of electronic devices and physical inactivity, poor neck postures and musculoskeletal disorders (MSD), which can negatively impact cervical spine health, are now on the rise. Current neck posture monitoring devices lack up to date features such as proactive, real-time feedback, adequate notification systems, comfort and adjustments. To fulfill the existing limitations, a smart neck posture monitoring IoMT device based on an ESP32 microcontroller and MPU6050 sensor is proposed. The proposed system raises a voice-over alert and sends a mobile notification alert whenever a bad posture is detected. It also allows us to visualize the changes in neck orientation with the help of ThingSpeak software. Our device aims to prevent possible neck posture deterioration by eliminating the disadvantages of a range of available solutions. It will contribute to the improvement of neck posture habits, minimizing potential MSDs and increasing user’s awareness of monitor postures.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Lightweight Sign Language Recognition Leveraging Google Mediapipe and Deep Neural Net
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The advent of technologies like Deep Learning has revolutionized human interaction, transcending language and disability barriers. Sign Language Recognition (SLR) systems have emerged as vital tools, facilitating seamless communication between individuals and between humans and machines through Interfaces. However, existing SLR systems pose significant challenges, including the demand for high accuracy, low latency, simplicity in development and deployment, lightweight design for edge compatibility, and efficient resource utilization during training. Addressing these challenges necessitates developing a system that balances training data accuracy, ease of training, and resource efficiency. Conventional Deep learning approaches often rely on high-dimensional image datasets for training HGR models, resulting in trade-offs between latency, accuracy, complexity, and resource requirements. To mitigate these challenges, this paper harnesses the capabilities of Google Mediapipe to extract a 21-point hand landmark vector from each training image. By leveraging this low-dimensional data, we train model that are accurate, lightweight, less complex, and exhibit low latency, making them compatible with edge devices. The hand gesture images were collected for several gestures, such as peace, okay, and stop. These images will be converted to landmark vectors using Mediapipe. These landmark points were used to train the Deep Neural Network architecture developed in Tensorflow. The model was trained with each hand gesture assigned with a common word in English and the proposed model was tested with a live webcam stream. The proposed model is developed in Python in the Google Colab IDE with the help of libraries and frameworks like OpenCV, Tensorflow and Google Mediapipe. The proposed model outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches by achieving an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 8 8 \%}$.

articleTitle: An Efficient Transfer-Learning based Approach for Crop Yield Prediction using Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: One of the most important ways in which humans engage with their natural surroundings is through crop production, which involves the cyclical translocation of carbon across the ecosystem. The computational efficiency remains a big barrier to the algorithm’s broad use, despite its benefits in mechanism and yield estimation robustness. This paper proposes a new hybrid approach to winter wheat yield estimation that combines the Crop-Biomass-Algorithm of Wheat (CBA-Wheat) with the Simple-Algorithm-for-Yield (SAFY) model and transfer-learning(TL). The approach enables calculation efficiency and acceptable accuracy. Using what they’ve learned from the SAFY model, the transfer learning algorithms can forecast wheat harvests. The main results demonstrated that: (1) With R2 of 0.83 and RMSE of 1.91 tha-1, respectively, the comparison of measured and anticipated AGB utilizing CBA-Wheat shows a virtuous correlation; (2) Compared to the other two yield estimation tests, TL with the ample recreation dataset expressively uses significantly less time. With a total of around 16,000 pixels to model, we needed to determine how well the data assimilation technique and TL performed in the absence of full simulation datasets. If the TL model can make production estimation more efficient, it will be a huge boon.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Deep Learning Models for Human Activity Recognition - Performance Evaluation and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced deep learning framework designed to enhance Human Activity Recognition (HAR) by leveraging the combined strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). HAR plays a crucial role in various applications, including surveillance, autonomous systems, and human-computer interaction. Despite significant advancements in machine learning, accurately recognizing and classifying human activities from video data remains challenging due to the complexity of spatio-temporal dependencies. Our proposed hybrid approach integrates 3D CNNs for efficient spatial feature extraction, ConvLSTMs to capture temporal dynamics, and GRUs to refine sequential learning, creating a robust model capable of handling complex and overlapping human actions. Extensive evaluations were conducted on two benchmark datasets, HMDB51 and UCF50, focused on 12 actions. The hybrid model achieved superior performance, with an accuracy of 96% on the UCF50 dataset and 95.4% on the HMDB51 dataset, surpassing traditional models such as LRCN, ConvLSTM, and 3D CNN in both precision and F1-score. This study highlights the effectiveness of hybrid spatio-temporal models in improving HAR accuracy, offering valuable insights for future research and practical applications in the field.

articleTitle: A New Cluster Decision Analysis Study based on EWM and Combined Regression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: In the context of the development of data science and big data technology, decision analysis has become quite important in many fields. In particular, in business management, financial market analysis, and the formulation of public policies, how to effectively analyze and make use of a large amount of data to make scientific and rational decisions has become an urgent problem. In these regards, cluster analysis is an important method of statistical analysis that helps a decision-maker get a better understanding of the structure of the data or patterns by organizing them into clusters in which objects that belong to the same cluster are similar to each other and much different from those that form other clusters. However, traditional clustering methods basically rely on single statistical or machine learning models, which often results in limitations and instability in the outcomes. Therefore, combining multiple methods to improve accuracy and reliability in decision analysis is a current research focus. In this respect, a new cluster decision analysis method is proposed in the present study, one that combines the Entropy Weight Method with combined regression analysis. The Entropy Weight Method is an objective weighting method aimed at determining the weights of indicators; it is very effective in reflecting variability and information content in every indicator. Combined regression analysis joins powers of these various regression models to be more pervasive and accurate in understanding relationships between variables. One can, therefore, fine-tune the precision of cluster analysis by such combined methodology and at the same time, enhance the interpretability and practicality of results. It will build up this new approach and apply it to the deep data analysis of certain fields, verifying the effectiveness and superiority of the application, and providing more scientific and reliable analytical tools for related decision-makers to make decisions in complex environments.

articleTitle: Bottom-Up Cracks Detection in Road Pavement in Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: In recent years, road crack detection is a significant task for detecting surface defects, road safety and road maintenance. But there is lack of approach that able to detect the concealed cracks especially bottom-up cracks, and this is challenging due to poor continuity of cracks, various crack’s widths, and low contrast among cracks and the surrounding pavement. The Artificial Neural Network (ANN) algorithm is proposed for detecting and classifying the structural health status of bottom-up crack in road pavements, which allows detecting surface defects and failures. The approach aims at collection of these signatures by utilizing acoustic-sensors, located at roadside, and also classification of SHS in pavements over the ANN approaches. The various Machine Learning (ML) classifiers such as Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), 2-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (2D-CNN), Support Vector Classifier (SVC) and Random Forest Classifier (RFC) are utilized as well as compared for the analysis of crack in road pavement. The experimental results illustrate the probability of associating with great accuracy $92.7 \%$ of MLP, $96.7 \%$ of 2D-CNN, $92.5 \%$ of RFC and ${9 9 . 3 \%}$ of SVC respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Digital Resource Library for Japanese Language Teaching based on Cloud Technology using BERT-NCF
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Recent days, the increasing demand for Japanese language instruction has created a need for comprehensive digital resources to support teaching and learning. A digital library provides accessible and engaging materials for educators and students. Traditional methods for building a digital resource library for Japanese language has faced significant challenges like the data contains irrelevant features and quality of text is poor. Therefore, this paper proposes Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers - Neural Collaborative Filtering (BERT-NCF) for building a digital resource library for Japanese language teaching which is employed on Jisho API dataset which consists of words, phrases and sentences of Japanese language. Then, the data is preprocessed by using Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK) approaches like tokenization, stop word removal, stemming and Lemmatization which improved the text quality and reduced noise. After that, the optimal features are extracted by using BERT which effectively eliminated the irrelevant features from data and model accuracy is improved by using Adam Weight decay (AdamW) optimizer. Finally, NCF is used to recommend useful personalized Japanese language learning resources by using obtained features. The proposed BERT-NCF achieved better results in terms of accuracy ($\mathbf{9 8. 5 0 \%}$), Precision (91.25%), Recall (92.49%), and F1 score (95.26%) when compared with existing BERT model.

articleTitle: Flight Trajectory Prediction and Analysis of Power Grid Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Using Variational Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: With the increasing popularity of power grid drones in power inspection, how to improve the accuracy of flight trajectory prediction has become a key challenge. Traditional prediction methods have problems with insufficient accuracy and limited generalization ability when dealing with complex and high-dimensional flight trajectory data. This paper introduces variational autoencoder (VAE) as a new machine learning algorithm for efficient prediction and analysis of the flight trajectory of power grid drones. VAE encodes and decodes flight trajectory data, learns its potential implicit representation, and thus generates more accurate future flight trajectory predictions. Experimental results show that the accuracy of flight trajectory prediction is increased to $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$ after using VAE. This study verifies the effectiveness of the VAE algorithm in power grid drone flight trajectory prediction, reveals its potential application in power grid operation management, and provides technical support and theoretical reference for improving power grid management efficiency and safety.

articleTitle: Hybrid Movie Recommendation System using Neural Collaborative Filtering with Gradient Decent and Association Rule Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: In recent days, most of the people are entertained by watching movies and shows, so developing a recommendation system help people across the world in saving the time to search for high rated movies. Usually, movies are recommended based on the user interests in the different movie genres such as horror, drama, romantic and comedy. Previous researchers suggested various methods for movie recommendation using Content Based Filtering (CBF), Collaborative Filtering (CF) which failed to predict the non-linear relationship recommendation due to the availability of many genres. To overcome this challenge, we proposed hybrid model namely Neural Collaborative Filtering (NCF) with gradient decent and Association Rule Mining (ARM). Initially, MovieLens dataset is employed and then data cleaning data organization is incorporated in pre-processing. Further, the features are extracted through the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) and Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) to convert the text data into numerical data and increase the performance respectively. Finally, the developed model was measured using Root mean square error (RMSE), precision, recall, and F 1 score. Hence, the proposed hybrid recommendation model provides higher accuracy value when compared to Knowledge-aware Attentional Neural Network (KANN).

Author Keywords: content based filtering latent semantic analysis

articleTitle: A Light Weight Deep Learning Framework for Brain Tumour Classification from Compressed MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The higher dimensionality of Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) poses challenges for storage, transmission, and computational efficiency when used with deep learning (DL) models for automated tumour classification. This paper introduces a novel lightweight DL framework that uses MobileNetV2 to classify brain tumours from discrete wavelet transform (DWT) compressed brain MRI images. The proposed framework is developed and deployed on a Raspberry Pi 4B single-board computer and achieves an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 4. 0 8 \%}$ for compressed images, compared to $\mathbf{9 3. 7 1 \%}$ for uncompressed images. The performance analysis of the developed model was equally impressive, with compressed images outperforming uncompressed images in terms of precision (93.41% vs. $\mathbf{9 3. 0 9 \%}$), recall ($\mathbf{9 2. 9 7 \%}$ vs. $\mathbf{9 2. 8 1 \%}$), and F1-score (92.98% vs. $\mathbf{9 2. 9 1 \%)}$. The results demonstrate that DWT compressed MRI images consistently perform well with the model, achieving near-perfect classification for the ‘No Tumor’ class and robust performance for glioma, pituitary, and meningioma classes.

articleTitle: Smart Water Management in Agriculture: Enhancing Crop Productivity with Restricted Boltzmann Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Effective water management in agriculture is crucial for sustainable food production in the face of water scarcity and climate change. The focus of this literature is on new methods and technology that aim to maximize water usage in agricultural activities and improve irrigation efficiency. Efficient water management practices are critical for increasing agricultural yields while lowering water wastage. By implementing water-saving measures and utilizing efficient irrigation systems, farmers can enhance yields while reducing pressure on scarce freshwater resources. Preprocessing, feature selection, and model training are all part of the suggested method. During the preprocessing phase, an Adaptive Inverse Normalization Layer is employed. The RFE methodology relies on a ranking algorithm that sorts the dataset from best to worst according to the attributes that are considered most important. Throughout training, the proposed approach utilized the RBM model without interruption. With a 93.21% average accuracy, this cutting-edge approach surpasses both DBN and KNN.

articleTitle: Priority of Requirements Sorting Method in Software Engineering Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Requirement priority is one of the core issues in software engineering, which directly determines the rational utilization of project resources, effective management of project risks, and the quality of the final product. This article constructs a requirement scoring model that describes the characteristics of requirements, proposes a software requirement prioritization method based on Non Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), and applies it to requirement prioritization in software engineering. Through a series of comparative experiments, the NSGA-II demand priority algorithm has a fast convergence speed, high project completion rate, and high project resource utilization rate. The experimental results indicate that the convergence process takes up to 478 milliseconds. In terms of resource utilization efficiency, NSGA-II is the best, with the highest resource utilization rate of $87.4 \%$, which can provide effective support for requirement management in software engineering.

articleTitle: Capsule Network with Long Short-Term Memory for Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Electrical Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The identification of fault types and their locations is crucial for power system when a fault occurs in the lines. Subsequently various type of faults and producing maximum capacity of electrical power grids is processing in the static mode. However, the electrical power transmission is access in static mode, dynamic power generated is failure to analysis the traditional mechanism. This paper proposed Capsule Network with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for detection various type of faults as parameters of the model to expand the scope of the fault identification. Data collected from the simulated three phase of the grid power that change in the voltages of current, which is enhance capsule network combined the LSTM in electrical power transmission system. The combination of capsule network and LSTM technique enhance the detection of different types of faults. The capsule network captures the spatial hierarchies and analysis relationship between various feature, while LSTM handle the temporal dependencies in grid power. The static and dynamic behaviours handle the capsule network and LSTM dynamically generation pattern of power grid data. The performance of proposed method is evaluated with various metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and f1-score metrics on grids power.

articleTitle: Virtual Twin Analytics: Advancing IoT Security through AI-Powered Software Informatics
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The Internet has grown in importance and impact over the years, causing people to become more reliant on it. The Internet has evolved into a major vector for cybercrime because to its ever-increasing user base. Over the last decade, the number of these computing systems—including desktops, laptops, smartphones, and the Internet of Things (IoT)—has skyrocketed. Among them, cell phones are practically integral to modern life. The popularity of web-based assaults has skyrocketed with the exponential growth in the number of individuals using the Internet. These web-based assaults are increasingly being combatted by security corporations. Unfortunately, new forms of these assaults are appearing all the time, making it hard for older security measures to stay up. Artificial intelligence (AI) is a source of optimism in the current cybersecurity landscape, offering a potential solution to the ever-changing digital dangers. The fast development of AI over the last decade has given rise to this optimism, because it is now impacting the expansion of every industry. With AI bringing so many advantages in every field, online security is one sector that just cannot afford to ignore it. This planned effort’s work represents an advance in that direction. Critical online security issues have been the focus of this proposed work’s study, which aims to address these issues using AI. Web security issues for desktop and mobile devices have been addressed in the proposed work. The planned work’s contributions to online security are as follows: The ‘MalCrawler’ web crawler is a targeted tool for finding and exploring the web. This crawler makes it easy to gather websites, particularly ones that are harmful. It does a better job of collecting dangerous websites than a typical crawler. Additionally, it is built to circumvent the evasion strategies used by rogue websites. The crawler’s ability to gather webpages—particularly dangerous ones—in order to provide datasets for ML-based analysis and solutions makes it a substantial addition to online security. Provides an in-depth examination of characteristics that may be used to categorize harmful websites. Data gain, pre-processing resource consumption, and prediction performance with various Conventional ML methods are some of the metrics used to assess these qualities. In addition, it suggests other conventional ML-based algorithms to better accurately anticipate dangerous websites by using these properties.

articleTitle: An Underwater Spam Detection Algorithm based on Enhanced YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: The present paper proposes an enhanced YOLOv8-based method for detecting underwater debris. The lightweight model YOLOv8n is selected as the baseline and optimized and improved in this way, our model can address the issues of inadequate detection, slow processing speed, and excessive model size in the previous approach. The paper enhances the model’s ability to focus on key features by incorporating the high-efficiency attention module, thereby enhancing model performance in complex underwater environments. Following the investigation into Ghost convolution and subsequent comparative tests, it has been resolved to substitute the standard convolution with Ghost convolution in the model’s neck region. This modification aims to enhance the model’s inference velocity and render the model more compact. Ultimately, Comparison and ablation studies on public data sets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and advancement of the method.

articleTitle: Enhanced ECG-Based Biometric Authentication using a Hybrid CNN-LSTM Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Reliability for sensitive applications is limited by flaws in traditional biometric systems, such as fingerprint, face, and iris identification, which include ease of spoofing, replication, and degradation over time. Using a hybrid deep learning framework that combines Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) provides a unique ECG-based biometric authentication system to address these problems. Enhanced security and accuracy are achieved by utilizing the unique and challenging-to-copy features of ECG signals. As the LSTM records temporal patterns and considerably enhances authentication efficiency, the CNN retrieves intricate features from unprocessed ECG data. As the experimental results show, the proposed CNNLNSTM framework outperforms conventional precision, recall, and error rates, achieving an impressive 98.5% accuracy. It’s a reliable option for real-time biometric authentication because of its high adaptability and scalability. Because it overcomes the drawbacks of earlier methods, the advanced technology provides a significant boost in biometric security.

articleTitle: Automated Crop Disease Detection and Classification using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Plant disease detection is crucial for ensuring food security and agricultural sustainability by enabling timely intervention to prevent crop losses. Recent advancements in machine learning and image processing have transformed plant pathology, offering efficient and accurate disease identification. This work involves collecting and pre-processing diverse plant image datasets, which are then resized and augmented using the FastAI library in Python to improve model generalization. A convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the ResNet architecture is trained via transfer learning to classify plant images as healthy or diseased. The trained model achieves high accuracy, establishing a reliable baseline for disease detection. It is integrated into a user-friendly interface with Tkinter, allowing users to classify plant images in real time via webcam or uploaded images. The system provides instant predictions on plant health and disease probability, with keyboard shortcuts for swift assessment of live camera feeds, enhancing decisionmaking for agricultural practitioners.

articleTitle: Dual Channel based Convolutional Neural Network based Protein–Ligand Interaction Prediction for Drug Design
publicationTitle: 2024 First International Conference on Software, Systems and Information Technology (SSITCON)
abstract: Nowadays, the drug discovery and drug design is developing to yield safe drugs constantly based on time, labor efficient way and cost. In drug discovery, the binding affinity and interaction strength among ligand and target protein are the main factors used for prediction. However, the existing Deep Learning (DL) based prediction approaches failed to predict the binding affinity between ligand and protein precisely. To overcome this problem, a Dual Channel based Convolutional Neural Network (DC-CNN) method is proposed for predicting binding affinity and interaction between protein and ligand for drug design. The proposed DC-CNN model which consists of two blocks that enhanced the prediction by capturing relationship (interaction) between protein and ligand.
